CT2.no_uplift: Improved internal controls but field evidence still blocked

cycles.A_question: Compare DA and online sequential filtering on exactly same ex ante regular bipartite opportunity graph
cycles.B_rivals: H_static DA sorting from preference and mutual feasibility; H_dynamic online thresholds add sorting over static greedy after opportunity matching; H_null differences explained by information timing
cycles.C_falsification: N400 200 men/women, k=20 and k=60 regular exposure graphs; 5 seeds, same fixed per-edge utility with Gaussian dyadic error sd=.08; three algorithms DA (full graph ranking; outside .05), greedy early accept (utility >=.05), adaptive sequential (q0=.8, qmin=.05, fatigue .015 per observed failure + .01 only for unilateral accept). Graph edges processed in same pre-drawn random schedule for sequential variants; DA sees all edges, explicitly informational advantage. Endpoints r,coverage,matched-mean utility,blocking edge count; invariants unique pairs, DA no blocking pairs, all matches on graph.
cycles.D_instrument: Paridad del conjunto de parejas potenciales, no de tiempo/información; contrast greedy vs dynamic strongest timing control. N total 400.
cycles.E_results: k20: DA r .863809 cover .960; greedy same order r -.007140 cover .962; adaptive same order r .377506 cover .348. k60: DA r .917013 cover .982; greedy r .035150 cover .986; adaptive r .711397 cover .805 (5 seeds/arm). DA 0 blocking pairs in all conditions after checker repair.
cycles.E_invalid_or_blocker: First run INVALID due blocking auditor transposed indices and yielded 1432 false blocking pairs; repaired in new frozen hash and rerun, failure preserved.
cycles.F_adversarial: DA has complete ranking over same graph while online only sees sequence; equal ex ante edges is not equal information. Greedy accepts early, destroying sorting; DA stability is built into its algorithm.
cycles.G_confirmation: No independent external confirmation; for synthetic tests 5 same-generator seeds, for documentary sources primary pages only
cycles.H_update: Compatibility of high sorting with pure preferences/matching confirmed within model; no uniqueness of adaptive threshold; timing and information crucial.
cycles.J_decision: STOP any claim that adaptive search is uniquely sufficient; prioritize calibrated theoretical comparison

cycles.A_question: Repair low-power N03 via balanced local pools, controlled distinct exposures
cycles.B_rivals: H0 observed local effects vanish with balanced composition and sufficient successful matches; H1 residual pool-size sorting remains
cycles.C_falsification: N1200 balanced sexes, pool sizes 100,300,1200, exactly T40 distinct scheduled encounters/personal until match (each pool has >=50 opposite); same q0=.82 fatigue=.015 rejection=.005; five seeds and same population per seed, randomized pool assignments. Pilot rule from prereg: 2 independent seeds to assess if min coverage >=40% and >=50 pairs per condition; otherwise stop without tuning parameters. Proceed with all five only if gate met. Record distribution of pairs/pool and effective exposures.
cycles.D_instrument: Identical potential exposures per agent pre-match, opportunities cease upon matching; pool compositions differ otherwise. Record denominator and power caveats.
cycles.E_results: Pilot seeds 1103,2207 both pass >=40% coverage and >=50 pairs/condition; completed 5 seeds. Pool100 r=.725609 coverage=.599; pool300 r=.740880 coverage=.603; pool1200 r=.736614 coverage=.594333. Size gradient not monotone and small against seed variation.
cycles.E_invalid_or_blocker: Prepilot N03 previous campaign was inconclusive due 1.3–1.6% coverage; current gate passed without adjusting q/T after observations.
cycles.F_adversarial: Same planned 40 distinct candidates, 50/50 sex in each pool; exits imply different realised encounters. Five seeds not a test of equivalence; do not claim zero effect or exact invariance.
cycles.G_confirmation: No independent external confirmation; for synthetic tests 5 same-generator seeds, for documentary sources primary pages only
cycles.H_update: Earlier large raw pool-size differences likely confounded by desynchronized opportunities/composition; under constraints no clear size gradient.
cycles.J_decision: Do not enlarge N without external geography/recommendation data; conditional STOP or new rival design

cycles.A_question: Asynchrony under exactly same bipartite edge graph and 40 planned evaluations per person
cycles.B_rivals: H0 ordering/exposure asymmetry changes outcomes only via realised exposure; H1 fixed reciprocal opportunity graph but timing generates differences
cycles.C_falsification: N400, 200/sex, k40 random regular bipartite graph, T40. Same score and pair-specific dyadic error sd=.06, q0=.8 fatigue=.015 by own unsuccessful views, no feedback after unilateral rejection (in async unresolved until second side view). Three variants: sync both view same edge at same round; async men evaluate edges in order, women a fixed shuffled offset order, likes persist; async with likes expiring after 5 ticks. 5 seeds with paired conditions and exact same prospective edges. Compare exposure-realisation, r,coverage, gap, distinct/mutually evaluated edges. Fix irrevocable left, exit on match. Ensure no duplicate matches.
cycles.D_instrument: Equal planned exposure graph, not equal realised degree among agents because exits endogenous; expiration changes feasible pair sets.
cycles.E_results: Same ex ante k40 regular graph N400 and 5 seeds: sync r=.632933 coverage=.616; async persistent r=.444042 coverage=.602; async expiry5 r=.395945 coverage=.566. Realised mutually evaluated edges differ due early exits.
cycles.E_invalid_or_blocker: No assertion errors on valid run; distinct prospective graph verified, temporal match state persisted.
cycles.F_adversarial: Equal planned edges is not equal realised exposures; mutable q by view and asynchrony affect the set of active agents and decision times. Expiration effect not independently isolated from match timing selection.
cycles.G_confirmation: No independent external confirmation; for synthetic tests 5 same-generator seeds, for documentary sources primary pages only
cycles.H_update: Asynchrony remains an active mechanism worth modelling, but not a clean causal attribution to app interface.
cycles.J_decision: BRANCH to equalised risk-set opportunities or formal Markov model, not extrapolate Tinder

cycles.A_question: Confirm July 2026 INE 20-39 sex counts, separate eligible users
cycles.B_rivals: National sex ratio for all ages distorts dating market; resident age counts still not pool of available willing heterosexual users
cycles.C_falsification: Obtain and validate official INE age sex 20-39 data via ECP national table/API; compare previous secondary 5,969,215 men and 5,677,941 women if available; look up civil status / cohabitation AND dating app activity by sex/age. If exact values inaccessible, mark DATA_BLOCKED rather than derive invented numbers.
cycles.D_instrument: Official provenance urls, query and date; documentary evidence not human experimental cycle.
cycles.E_results: Official INE ECP 1-7-2026 49,801,559 total, 24,462,607 men and 25,338,952 women checked. National table 59583 identified, but requested 20–39 sex-by-age 2026 cells could not be retrieved via accessible CSV/API. Island table 59662 correctly rejected as national source. Dating-market eligible denominator not observed.
cycles.E_invalid_or_blocker: Age-sex 20-39 exact July secondary estimate not upgraded to official; DATA_BLOCKED for requested cross-tab and activity measure.
cycles.F_adversarial: Resident, legally single, not in partnership, heterosexual, willing to date, app-active are different populations; crude national sex ratio can reverse sign in age subset.
cycles.G_confirmation: No independent external confirmation; for synthetic tests 5 same-generator seeds, for documentary sources primary pages only
cycles.H_update: Use official age-sex table only when numerically acquired; do not use total Spain as mating population or Tinder penetration proxy.
cycles.J_decision: REQUEST appropriate official data with citation/CSV provenance before any Spanish calibration

cycles.A_question: Obtain modern cross-tab of partners' education and calculate independence-adjusted homogamy
cycles.B_rivals: Raw diagonal may reflect marginal educational composition, not preferences or matching process
cycles.C_falsification: Inspect official marriage table 60268 national year 2023 or latest available and CSV for joint educational levels; download parse if technically accessible; otherwise report accessible schema + DATA_BLOCKED, do not fabricate counts. If accessible compute observed diagonal, expected independent sum(row_i col_i/N), O/E and simple permutation-preserving marginals; no link between marriages and Tinder matches.
cycles.D_instrument: Disclosure years, data definition, unknown/missing education, no inference into apps.
cycles.E_results: INE table 60268 identified, with explicit two-sided education levels of male/female spouses and period 2016–2023 in accessible view; webpage selected no cells and CSV/px endpoints inaccessible. No cross-tab computed.
cycles.E_invalid_or_blocker: MATRIX_BLOCKED, no joint counts; observed diagonal 2001 cannot substitute for modern matrix.
cycles.F_adversarial: A diagonal is not excess homogamy absent independence given marginal education distributions; marriage and swipe have different outcome and selection.
cycles.G_confirmation: No independent external confirmation; for synthetic tests 5 same-generator seeds, for documentary sources primary pages only
cycles.H_update: Formula O=sum diag(nij)/N; E=sum ri*ci/N²; O/E only after valid counts; strata age/year and exclude or separately report 'No consta'.
cycles.J_decision: SEEK accessible 2023 matrix and weights, stop synthetic validation claim

cycles.A_question: Review empirically observable reputation signal of online dating rejection
cycles.B_rivals: Private swipe/ghosting vs observable network cues vs truly global public rejection; reputational status loss cannot be stipulated empirically
cycles.C_falsification: Review peer-reviewed field or diary studies with dates, sample designs, limitations; formal DAG with direct private signal versus observable-to-third-party; define valid tests, confidentiality and risks; stronger baseline none/private/local/public tied to actual visibility. No collecting real individuals' ratings.
cycles.D_instrument: Document only, no intervention or status penalty measured in human dataset.
cycles.E_results: Campaioli et al 2025 diary: 8 participants for one month, awareness cues after rejection and surveillance; van der Zanden & Schokkenbroek 2024 two cross-sectional surveys, first n=177, examines rejection types/reasons/hurt. Neither identifies a general causal objective status drop per rejection.
cycles.E_invalid_or_blocker: No empirical probability of third-party knowledge of swipes or quantified reputation penalty extracted.
cycles.F_adversarial: Private swipe decisions generally may not be observable; direct effect of rejection on self differs from publicly transmitted reputation; sharing may cause risks to users.
cycles.G_confirmation: No independent external confirmation; for synthetic tests 5 same-generator seeds, for documentary sources primary pages only
cycles.H_update: Model channel R -> exposure Z to third parties -> perceived value, requiring empirical evidence of Z. Include private-information negative control and safeguards.
cycles.J_decision: STOP global objective status penalty as empirical statement; future privacy-safe research

global_J: STOP_CAMPAIGN_AND_DO_NOT_USE_MORE_UNAUTHORISED_CYCLES. High-value next evidence is external active-user data, education cross-tab and a risk-set matched comparator.
